messages:
maria: Heads-up — last night us-west had a burst of GPU flares during the 02:00 maintenance window, ~8 noisy alerts in 30m, Pager got paged twice. TL;DR: we should revisit paging vs ticketing thresholds.
ken: I saw the noise. Most were single-instance node recoveries, not cluster level. Paging for those is overkill.
jess: Agreed. We should only page when it impacts service-level traffic or >N nodes in a pool.
tim: Propose: page when cluster_gpu_flares_total by pool > 3 over 5m OR p99.latency crosses SLO + any active rollout. Otherwise create a ticket.
maria: +1. Also want adaptive baselines per-region — us-west has different normal flake than eu-central.
ken: How about using anomaly suppression: compare to 7-day median for that pool, only escalate if > 2x baseline and sustained for 10m. That would cut down recurring transient noise.
sre-rotation: We also need to avoid double-paging during deploys. Suggest auto-snooze for alerts tagged with `deploy=true` for the deploy window unless severity=critical.
ops-bot: Reminder: current rule `GPU_FLAIR_HIGH` pages immediately with `for: 0m`. We can change to `for: 5m` + grouping by `pool,region`.
maria: Example alert draft I sketched — can we review?
maria: ```yaml
groups:
  - name: gpu-alerts
    rules:
      - alert: GPU_FLARE_CLUSTER
        expr: sum by(pool, region) (increase(gpu_flare_total[5m])) > 3
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: page
        annotations:
          summary: "Multiple GPU flares in {{ $labels.pool }} ({{ $labels.region }})"
      - alert: GPU_FLARE_INSTANCE
        expr: increase(gpu_flare_total[5m]) > 0
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: ticket
        annotations:
          summary: "Single-instance GPU flare in {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
ken: That looks good. Two comments: (1) set `group_by` to `pool,region` in Alertmanager so we bundle per-pool. (2) Add a suppression rule that if `deploy=true` and deploy_start <= now <= deploy_end then route to ticketing.
tim: Also add SLO burn rate check: if gpu-related errors are causing SLO burn rate > 0.5 then escalate to page regardless of node count.
jess: For operational safety, weekends should still page for cluster-wide incidents, but small one-offs go to a ticket. No blanket quieting windows.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: infra/driver-rollout/us-west at 2026-03-14T01:45Z (tag: driver-v2). Auto-snooze enabled for associated alerts.
maria: Action items: 1) Ken to add group_by and suppression rule in Alertmanager. 2) Tim to wire SLO burn rate -> alert pipeline as override. 3) Jess to update runbook with new paging thresholds. 4) Ops-bot to change `GPU_FLAIR_HIGH` to the two-rule pattern above.
ken: I'll open a PR for alertmanager + rules, target EOD. will add tests that simulate 7-day baseline and deploy tag.
sre-rotation: Add me to the oncall rota change if this lands before Friday. Want to validate with a canary window.
maria: Thanks all. If folks want to experiment with suppression thresholds, push a temp rule in `eng-sre/dev` and we'll monitor via the SLO dashboard.
ops-bot: Note: new grafana panel link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/gpu-flare-slo — use this to validate burn rate.
ken: I'll post the PR and a short changelog in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
